rows.title: Two-State Continuous-Time Markov Kernel

maturity_record.invariant: Positive two-state rates define a nonnegative transition matrix with every row summing to one for nonnegative time.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The state carrier is Boolean, both rates are strictly positive, and time is nonnegative. This is an exact two-state kernel rather than a general continuous-time Markov-chain construction.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The benchmark rates seven tenths and three tenths give decay rate one and a nonuniform stationary law.

theorem fep149_twoStateSemigroup_rowSum
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (time : ℝ) (source : Bool) :
    ∑ target, rates.transition time source target = 1
qualified_declaration_statements.fep149_twoStateSemigroup_nonnegative:
theorem fep149_twoStateSemigroup_nonnegative
    (rates : TwoStateRates) {time : ℝ} (hTime : 0 ≤ time)
    (source target : Bool) :
    0 ≤ rates.transition time source target

rows.statement_review: Explicit positive Bool jump rates a,b give stationary masses b/(a+b),a/(a+b) and transition entries built from rho=exp(-(a+b)t). Row sums1 hold for all real t; nonnegativity requires t>=0. Benchmark a=.7,b=.3 has decay1 and stationary true mass.7.

The owner additionally already constructs a general finite-rate-generator matrix-exponential semigroup by uniformisation, proves nonnegativity/master equations, and identifies its two-state specialization with these formulas; do not call general finite-state semigroup construction absent. Continuous path-process existence is different.

rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: For t<0 rho>1 and off-diagonal entries become negative although row sums1 remain. Zero rates lie outside TwoStateRates even if some limiting chains exist.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 010 native reversible kernels and finite149 explicit analytic transitions are distinct; its foundation now includes a proved general finite-generator identification, not a PDE theorem.

maturity_record.invariant: The exact two-state transition matrices satisfy the Chapman–Kolmogorov additive semigroup law entrywise.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Both times are nonnegative and rates are strictly positive. Composition is the finite Boolean matrix sum and no path-space or general generator existence theorem is inferred.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Positive unequal rates and positive times produce nonidentity kernels whose matrix product still equals the transition at summed time.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep151_twoStateSemigroup_add:
theorem fep151_twoStateSemigroup_add
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (left right : ℝ) (source target : Bool) :
    rates.transition (left + right) source target =
      ∑ middle,
        rates.transition left source middle *
          rates.transition right middle target

rows.statement_review: The closed-form transition satisfies entrywise Chapman–Kolmogorov for all real left/right times; nonnegative times give the probability-kernel semigroup interpretation.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The current maturity assumption unnecessarily restricts the algebraic statement to nonnegative times. Negative times retain the matrix group identity but lose positivity. Existing certifiedSemigroup and uniformised_transition_eq bind the finite-generator semigroup; no sample-path or PDE inference follows.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Benchmark rates at two positive times log2 have rho factors1/2,1/2 and summed-time rho1/4; actual nonidentity kernels compose.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: A generic normalized family of kernels need not satisfy additive semigroup composition. Negative-time entries can be negative despite the identity.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 006 discrete iterate semigroup and151 real-time analytic matrix law are different carriers; conversion must use actual semigroup/selected-time definitions.

rows.title: Two-State Continuous-Time Master Equation

maturity_record.invariant: Every transition entry is differentiable and its derivative equals both the generator-times-transition and transition-times-generator finite sums.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The generator and transition matrices are the maintained explicit Boolean formulas. This proves the forward and backward master equations for one two-state semigroup, not a general CTMC existence theorem.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Positive unequal rates give nonzero off-diagonal derivatives away from stationarity and exercise both left and right generator products.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep152_twoStateSemigroup_hasDerivAt for all four entries.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep152_twoStateSemigroup_hasDerivAt:
theorem fep152_twoStateSemigroup_hasDerivAt
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (time : ℝ) (source target : Bool) :
    HasDerivAt (fun candidate ↦ rates.transition candidate source target)
        (∑ middle,
          rates.generator source middle * rates.transition time middle target)
        time ∧
      HasDerivAt (fun candidate ↦ rates.transition candidate source target)
        (∑ middle,
          rates.transition time source middle * rates.generator middle target)
        time

rows.statement_review: Each actual transition entry has HasDerivAt equal to both Q*P(t) and P(t)*Q, with the stated finite matrix index order. It holds for real t, including0.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: These are explicit forward/backward master equations, not supplied symbolic vector fields. Row-generator convention and multiplication order must be preserved. The existing general matrix-exponential finite-generator owner supplies further actual content, but no continuous-state Fokker–Planck/PDE theorem is asserted.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: At time0, false→true derivative a=.7 and true→false derivative b=.3, diagonals their negative row rates.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Transposing row-generator convention changes products/distribution evolution; arbitrary supplied Q/P do not satisfy these derivatives merely from row normalization.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 043 scalar derivative certificates and152 matrix-entry analytic derivatives are related techniques, not a carrier-free equivalence.

novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds an explicit rate generator, real-time derivatives, and left/right matrix products without claiming a general CTMC existence theorem.

rows.title: Continuous-Time Stationarity and Detailed Balance

maturity_record.invariant: The explicit stationary law is invariant under every nonnegative-time transition and satisfies detailed balance entrywise.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Both rates are strictly positive and time is nonnegative. Reversibility is proved only for this exact two-state family and does not cover driven or nonequilibrium generators.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Unequal benchmark rates produce a nonuniform stationary law while still balancing the two opposing fluxes.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep153_twoStateSemigroup_stationary and fep153_twoStateSemigroup_detailedBalance.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep153_twoStateSemigroup_stationary:
theorem fep153_twoStateSemigroup_stationary
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (time : ℝ) (target : Bool) :
    (∑ source,
        rates.stationaryLaw source * rates.transition time source target) =
      rates.stationaryLaw target
qualified_declaration_statements.fep153_twoStateSemigroup_detailedBalance:
theorem fep153_twoStateSemigroup_detailedBalance
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (time : ℝ) (source target : Bool) :
    rates.stationaryLaw source * rates.transition time source target =
      rates.stationaryLaw target * rates.transition time target source

rows.statement_review: The explicit stationary law is invariant and satisfies detailed balance for every real-time transition formula; probability interpretation uses t>=0.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: Positive rates imply unique nonzero stationary masses in this model. This is a reversible equilibrium family, not a driven NESS or arbitrary-generator detailed-balance theorem. Algebraic stationarity at negative t does not make a probability transition.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: At benchmark rates, opposing stationary infinitesimal fluxes .3*.7 and .7*.3 agree, and both finite-time transitions balance.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: A directed3-cycle generator elsewhere is stationary but not detailed balanced. Stationarity alone cannot imply these pairwise identities.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 010 reversibility⇒invariance is generic native content;153 supplies an actual analytic two-state family and explicit invariant law.

novelty_record.new_invariant: The exact two-state stationary law is invariant at every nonnegative time and satisfies entrywise detailed balance.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Extends discrete reversible-kernel laws to an explicit continuous-time semigroup with unequal positive rates.

touching_relations.rationale: The nonuniform stationary law satisfies exact continuous-time detailed balance, alongside the original native reversible-kernel stationarity theorem.

rows.title: Exact Two-State Exponential Relaxation

maturity_record.invariant: The true-state mass of any initial Boolean law relaxes toward stationarity by the exact factor exp(-(a+b)t).
maturity_record.assumption_review: Rates are positive, time is nonnegative, and prediction uses the explicit two-state transition. This is exact finite-state relaxation, not a mixing theorem for arbitrary chains.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The benchmark point mass differs from the nonuniform stationary law, so the decaying deviation starts nonzero.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep154_twoStateRelaxation_exact and fep154_benchmarkInitial_nonstationary.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep154_twoStateRelaxation_exact:
theorem fep154_twoStateRelaxation_exact
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (initial : FiniteLaw Bool) (time : ℝ) :
    rates.trueMass initial time - rates.stationaryTrue =
      rates.rho time * (initial true - rates.stationaryTrue)

rows.statement_review: For any initial Bool law and real time, true-mass deviation from stationaryTrue equals rho(t) times its initial deviation. This is an exact relaxation identity; natively normalized prediction uses nonnegative time.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: Positive decay gives forward-time exponential relaxation, not an arbitrary-chain mixing-rate result. At negative time the algebraic mass formula may leave[0,1]. The benchmark initial point mass is genuinely nonstationary.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Benchmark initial false point mass has initial deviation-7/10; at t=log2 deviation-7/20.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Initial=stationary gives zero deviation at every time. Negative time magnifies rather than relaxes deviation.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 020 discrete recurrence has a geometric iteration factor;154 gives the explicit continuous-time exponential factor on the same two-state-style scope without automatic timescale identification.

rows.title: Exact Two-State Quadratic Lyapunov Decay

maturity_record.invariant: Squared deviation from stationarity decays by exp(-2(a+b)t), and its exact derivative is minus twice the decay rate times the Lyapunov value.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The Lyapunov function is the scalar square of the true-state mass deviation for the explicit two-state semigroup. It is not a general entropy-production or physical free-energy theorem.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The benchmark nonstationary point mass has a strictly negative Lyapunov derivative at time zero.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of all three fep-155 declarations, including the strict benchmark derivative.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep155_twoStateLyapunov_exact:
theorem fep155_twoStateLyapunov_exact
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (initial : FiniteLaw Bool) (time : ℝ) :
    rates.lyapunov initial time =
      rates.rho time ^ 2 *
        (initial true - rates.stationaryTrue) ^ 2
qualified_declaration_statements.fep155_twoStateLyapunov_hasDerivAt:
theorem fep155_twoStateLyapunov_hasDerivAt
    (rates : TwoStateRates) (initial : FiniteLaw Bool) (time : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (rates.lyapunov initial)
      (-2 * rates.decayRate * rates.lyapunov initial time) time

rows.statement_review: Squared true-mass deviation equals rho(t)^2 times initial squared deviation and has derivative -2*(a+b)*V(t). Benchmark initial false point mass gives V0=49/100 and derivative-49/50.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The function is a quadratic Lyapunov diagnostic, not physical entropy, thermodynamic free energy or a universal entropy-production rate. At stationary initial law derivative0, so strictness needs nonstationarity.
